 Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, learned counsel for the 
petitioner. 
 Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned Deputy Advocate 
General for the State of Uttarakhand. 
 The petitioner has preferred this writ petition in 
public interest to seek a direction to the 
respondents for establishment of the Lokayukta
Institution and enforcement of the Lokayukta Act, 
2014, and to make appointment of the Chairman / 
Members of the Lokayukta Institution. 
 Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that 
the respondents may be directed to file the latest 
report with regard to enforcement of the aforesaid 
Act. He further submits that the State is reportedly 
spending crores of rupees every year without the 
Institution of Lokayukta being operational. 
 We direct the respondents to file an additional  affidavit disclosing the status with regard to 
establishment of the Lokayukta Institution. It 
should also be disclosed what is the expenditure 
incurred on the said Institution since inception 
year-wise upto 31st March, 2023. The affidavit be 
filed within three weeks. 
 List on 08.05.2023. 
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J) (Vipin Sanghi, CJ)

orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Vipin Sanghi,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Rakesh Thapliyal
orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND 
AT NAINITAL
HON’BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE SRI VIPIN SANGHI
AND 
HON’BLE SRI JUSTICE RAKESH THAPLIYAL
27TH JUNE, 2023
WRIT PETITION (PIL) No. 161 OF 2021
Between: 
Ravi Shankar Joshi. 
…Petitioner
and 
State of Uttarakhand and another. 
…Respondents
Counsel for the petitioner. : Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, learned 
counsel for the petitioner.
Counsel for respondents. : Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned Deputy 
Advocate General for the State of 
Uttarakhand. 
ORDER : (per Sri Vipin Sanghi, C.J.)
An affidavit has been filed by Shri Lalit Mohan 
Rayal, Additional Secretary, Department of Good 
Governance, Eradication of Corruption and Public 
Services, Government of Uttarakhand, in terms of our
order dated 17.03.2023. 
2. The affidavit discloses that, initially, the Uttar 
Pradesh Lokayukta and Up-Lokayukta Act, 1975 was 
made applicable to the State of Uttarakhand, on its 
creation, and that Hon’ble (Retd.) Justice S.H.A. Raza  2
was appointed as the 1st Lokayukta, and upon his 
superannuation on 23.10.2008, Hon’ble (Retd.) Justice 
M.M. Ghildiyal was appointed as the Lokayukta on 
01.11.2008. Vide notification dated 24.09.2013, the 
Uttarakhand Lokayukta Act, 2011 was brought into force
and, in terms of Section 36(1) of the said Act, the Uttar 
Pradesh Lokayukta and Up-Lokayukta Act, 1975 stood 
repealed, insofar as, its application in State of 
Uttarakhand is concerned. Consequently, the term of 
Hon’ble (Retd.) Justice M.M Ghildiyal, as Lokayukta,
came to an end. Since then, there is no Lokayukta 
appointed in the State of Uttarakhand. 
3. The affidavit further discloses that the 
Uttarakhand Lokayukta Act, 2014 was enacted on 
26.02.2014, and, with that, the Uttarakhand Lokayukta 
Act, 2011 was repealed. The said Act was further 
amended vide notification dated 23.12.2014, and the 
Uttarakhand Lokayukta (Amendment) Act, 2014 was 
brought into force, which, inter alia, stated that the said 
Act shall come into force from the date of appointment 
of the Lokayukta. Since no Lokayukta has been 
appointed under the said Act, the Act of 2014 has not 
come into force. This is despite the fact that the Search 
Committee, constituted under the said Act, has made  3
recommendations, but they have not been acted upon. 
The affidavit further discloses that a Bill was presented 
to the State Legislature for enactment of the 
Uttarakhand Lokayukta Act, 2017, but the said Bill has 
not been passed till date. Pertinently, it was informed to 
the Supreme Court, as early as on 10.01.2018, that a 
new enactment, pertaining to appointment of Lokayukta,
has been introduced in the State Legislative Assembly, 
when the Supreme Court was hearing WPPIL (Civil) No. 
57/2016, Ashwani Kumar (Vice Chairman) v. State 
of Uttarakhand. That assurance, given to the Supreme 
Court, has remained unimplemented till date.
4. Section 63 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 
2013 mandates that “every State shall establish a body 
to be known as the Lokayukta for the State, if not so 
established, constituted or appointed, by a law made by 
the State Legislature, to deal with complaints relating to 
corruption against certain public functionaries, within a 
period of one year from the date of commencement of 
this Act”. 
5. The purport of the aforesaid Section 63 is 
that, even if the State Legislature does not enact a law  4
for appointment of a Lokayukta, such Lokayukta shall be 
appointed under the provisions of the Lokpal and 
Lokayuktas Act, 2013. Therefore, in our view, it is no 
excuse for the State Government to state that, as there 
is no State Legislation in respect of appointment of a 
Lokayukta, the State Government is under no obligation 
to make appointment of the Lokayukta under the Lokpal 
and Lokayuktas Act, 2013. 
6. We, therefore, direct the State Government to 
forthwith proceed to make appointment of a Lokayukta 
in the State, positively within the next eight weeks
under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013. 
7. The affidavit also discloses the shocking state 
of affairs with regard to the expenditure incurred in the 
Office of the Lokayukta. It is disclosed that till 
31.03.2023, in respect of the Office of the Lokayukta, 
the budget allocated was Rs. 36,95,40,563/-, out of 
which the Lokayukta office has utilized a sum of Rs.
29,73,99,044/-. The detailed break-up is given in 
Annexure B-2 of the affidavit, which reads as follows :- 5
8. It is further disclosed that the services of 09 
employees, out of 24, of the Lokayukta Office, are 
temporarily being used in the Uttarakhand Real Estate 
Regulatory Authority (RERA) and the Uttarakhand Real 
Estate Appellate Tribunal (REAT). There is no disclosure 
as to what is the fate of the remaining 15 employees 
appointed in the Office of the Lokayukta, who have been 
drawing salaries. It is a matter of grave concern that 
the public exchequer is being burdened with such heavy  6
expenditures, even though the Office of the Lokayukta in 
the State is defunct, since the year 2013. 
9. We, therefore, direct the State not to incur
even a single rupee towards the Office of the Lokayukta 
till the appointment of the Lokayukta has been made. 
No further expenditure shall be incurred in the name of 
the Office of the Lokayukta by the State henceforth. 
10. The State shall file a further affidavit,
disclosing the names and designations of all the 24 
employees appointed in the Office of the Lokayukta, as 
well as the salaries drawn by them, and the manner in 
which their services are being utilized. An affidavit in 
this regard shall be filed within three weeks. 
11. List on 10.08.2023.
________________
VIPIN SANGHI, C.J.
__________________
RAKESH THAPLIYAL, J.
Dt: 27th June, 2023
Rahul

Hon’ble Vipin Sanghi, C.J.
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, learned counsel for the 
petitioner. 
2. Mr. Sunil Khera, learned Deputy Advocate 
General for the State of Uttarakhand. 
IA/7/2023
3. By this application, the respondents seek 
extension of time for compliance of our order dated 
27.06.2023. 
4. We have considered the said application. The 
respondents have asked for another six months’ time 
to report compliance of our aforesaid order. In our 
view, the same is not justified, and the respondents 
should complete the process of appointing the 
Lokayukta within three months from today. No further 
extension shall be granted. 
5. The application stands disposed of accordingly. 
IA/5/2023
6. By this application, the respondents seek 
modification of our order dated 27.06.2023. 
7. We are not inclined to modify our order, with 
regard to payment of salary to the staff claimed to 
have been deployed in the office of the Lokayukta. We 
fail to understand, as to what the said staff comprising 
of 17 persons, is doing in the Office of the Lokayukta, 
which is completely defunct. The payment of salary to 
such persons, from the office of the Lokayukta, is a  complete wasteful expenditure of public money. We, 
therefore, reject the request made. However, it shall 
be open to the respondents to post all such employees 
in such other departments, wherever their work is 
required on deputation, or otherwise, and they may be 
paid salaries from the departments, where they serve. 
8. List on 05.03.2024.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) (Vipin Sanghi, C.J.)

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS 
07.11.2023 WPPIL No. 161 of 2021 
Sri Manoj Kumar Tiwari, A.C.J.
Sri Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Karthik Jayashankar, learned counsel for the 
petitioner. 
2. Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned Chief Standing Counsel 
assisted by Mr. Gajendra Tripathi, learned Standing 
Counsel for the State- respondents. 
Modification Application (IA No.09 of 2023)
3. Co-ordinate Bench of this Court had passed 
interim order on 27.06.2023, directing the State not to 
incur any expenditure towards the Office of Lokayukta 
till the appointment of the Lokayukta is made. 
4. State has moved an application seeking 
modification of the said order. 
5. Learned Chief Standing Counsel submits that 
there are as many as 16 regular employees serving in 
the establishment of Lokayukta, who have not been 
paid any salary since July, 2023. He further points out 
that one employee, namely, Gopal Singh Bisht, retired 
on 31.10.2023, and before his retirement, there were 
17 employees serving in the office of Lokayukta. He 
further submits that pension and other retiral dues to 
Gopal Singh Bisht could also not be released because 
of the restraint order. 
6. It is further submitted that the work of 
renovation of office building of Lokayukta is 
undergoing, and due to restraint order passed by this 
Court, renovation work of the office building of  Lokayukta is hampered. He further submits that bills 
regarding electricity, telephone, water supply etc., and 
the bills regarding fuel and maintenance of official 
vehicles are also pending. 
7. Having regard to the problem faced by the 
regular employees working in the establishment of 
Lokayukta, and also with a view to ensure that 
functioning of the office of Lokayukta is not hampered, 
we allow the modification application, and permit the 
State to make payment of salary to regular 
employees, out of the budget already allocated. State 
shall also be at liberty to pay pending dues towards 
electricity, telephone and water supply etc. to the 
concerned agencies, during the current financial year, 
i.e. upto 31.03.2024. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, A.C.J.) 
 07.11.2023 07.11.2023 
NISHANT

petitioner. 
2. Mr. Gajendra Tripathi, learned Standing Counsel for 
the State.
3. On 27.06.2023, the Court noted with concern that the 
mandate of law for appointing a Lokayukta in the State was 
not being followed, whereas heavy expenditure was being 
incurred towards the Establishment of Lokayukta. Since 
thereafter, repeated orders have been passed and every 
time the State is seeking time to apprise the Court of the 
status of the proceedings relating to appointment of 
Lokayukta.
4. It is pertinent to note here that State in its affidavit 
dated 25.06.2025 stated that the process of appointment of
Lokayukta is on verge of completion; however, so far the 
process has not been completed. 
5. Learned State Counsel prays for further time to 
apprise the Court of the present status of the selection 
process.
6. While recording our displeasure, we grant two weeks’ 
further time to the State Counsel to apprise the Court of the 
present status. 
7. List on 01.04.2026.
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)

3. A co-ordinate bench vide order dated 
16.06.2026, extended the interim order dated 
07.11.2023, for a further period of six months. 
We are informed that the ministerial staff of the 
Office of Lokayukta has not been paid salary 
since last several months. The employees 
cannot be made to suffer because of delay on 
the part of the State in holding selection for 
appointment to the post of Lokayukta.
4. In such view of the matter, we extent the 
interim order dated 07.11.2023 till end of 
current financial year and permit the State to 
release salary of regular employees serving in 
the Office of Lokayukta out of the budget 
already allocated. State shall also be at liberty  to pay pending dues towards electricity, 
telephone and water supply etc. to the 
concerned agency for the current financial year.
5. State Counsel submits that the rules have 
now been notified on 25th August 2026, known 
as “The Uttarakhand Lokayukta Search 
Committee, Determination of Functions Rules,
2026”. He seeks two weeks’ time to get further 
necessary instructions in the matter.
6. On his request, list the matter on 
04.11.2026.
